text: 🇲🇽🏭 Plan México accelerates: national content, well-paid jobs, and value chains built at home. The government is speeding up its National Industrialization and Shared Prosperity Strategy, tied to the 2027 economic package. Its six pillars: more national and regional content in strategic sectors; well-paid manufacturing and innovation jobs; greater local value-added in supply chains; "polos de bienestar" and industrial corridors; clear investment priorities; and continental regional integration — a bet on producing more of what Mexico consumes. Mexico News Daily

🇲🇽🌎 Sheinbaum draws the red line in the tariff talks with Washington: sovereignty. "We will not sign anything that affects our sovereignty and our economy." Ahead of talks with U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, President Sheinbaum said Mexico's limit in the T-MEC and tariff negotiations is what it considers non-negotiable. Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard called the meeting "cordial" and traveled to Washington to continue; Mexico is pressing to cut U.S. tariffs on steel, aluminum and autos. No deal yet. Infobae

🇲🇽🏭 Record jobs and the OECD's lowest unemployment after Japan — under U.S. tariffs. "Our adversaries insist the Mexican economy is doing badly — but no. Every indicator shows we're doing well... we're the country with the fewest tariffs in the world. But we're doing well." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 11 The IMSS posted a record 22,798,473 formal jobs in August; the OECD again ranked Mexico's unemployment the lowest after Japan — even amid the new U.S. tariff policy.

🚨🇲🇽 Migration across Mexico's northern border fell from ~20,000 a day to about 300. "They're commercial drones, used to spot the Border Patrol or the U.S. Navy that President Trump put on the border so people can cross illegally. It's not right either... And migration has fallen enormously." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 11 In December 2023 nearly 20,000 people crossed daily; now it's 300–350, met by CBP and returned. Mexico keeps 10,000 National Guard and 3,300 troops on the border in mirror operations with the U.S.

🔥🇲🇽 The opposition is in Europe asking for intervention — during Mexico's independence month. "While the electoral season begins, they're in Europe. That has its symbolism — even more so now that we're about to celebrate the Grito de Independencia." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 11 A reporter read the words of José María Gutiérrez Estrada — the man who led the delegation begging Maximilian of Habsburg to come rule Mexico — as the PAN's leadership travels to Europe seeking help to free Ernesto Rufo. History rhymes.

🇲🇽✊ 25,000 "smart watches" that reach the police in a minute — Chiapas's Mujer Segura. "With one press of the button it sends a signal to the C5, and the response is almost immediate." — Gov. Eduardo Ramírez, Mañanera, Sept 11 The model was designed by Chiapas's own young women and students. More than 25,000 watches have been handed out, focused on municipalities under gender-violence alerts. August saw the fewest femicides on record in the state.

🇲🇽🎨 Chiapas halved illiteracy — and won UNESCO's Confucius Prize for how it did it. "Teaching people to read is an act of love. Literacy is the people's liberation." — Gov. Eduardo Ramírez, taking up President Sheinbaum's call, Mañanera, Sept 11 250,000 people learned to read using the bilingual "Matías de Córdoba" method across five Indigenous languages, taught by members of their own communities. Six of ten who couldn't read were women; in Indigenous towns, eight of ten.

🇲🇽🔍 Chiapas cut intentional homicides by 64% — 2026 is its least violent year since 2015. "People feel safer in Chiapas today than they did two years ago." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 11 Daily homicides fell from 2.5 (Dec 2024) to 0.9 (Aug 2026). High-impact crimes are down 44% and vehicle theft 68%. The state that was among Mexico's most violent in 2024 now ranks second on the national Peace Index.

🇲🇽🛒 <u>MEXICO'S E-COMMERCE NOW OUTWEIGHS ITS ENTIRE AIRLINE SECTOR</u>

Mercado Libre's ecosystem moved 106.4 billion pesos through Mexico's economy in 2025 — 0.4% of GDP, edging out the country's entire air-transport sector (0.36%), per El Economista. It now sustains 136,800 jobs (34,300 direct) and more than a million small and medium businesses, and the company is committing a record 4.6 billion dollars to Mexico in 2026 — 30% more than last year, its largest bet yet in the country.

🇲🇽📚 <u>MEXICO ZEROES OUT VAT ON BOOKS TO PUT READING WITHIN REACH</u>

Mexico has moved books from a plain tax exemption to a full zero-VAT rate — letting publishers and bookstores reclaim the IVA on their costs while retail prices stay put, at a fiscal cost of about 200 million pesos a year. President Sheinbaum framed it as support for "all publishers," not one house; SAT chief Antonio Martínez Dagnino said the refunds are "support for all people and companies." The measure answers years of advocacy from the Brigada para Leer en Libertad and the Fondo de Cultura Económica.
